Verified the real Alpaca link completely and confirmed the system is running and waiting for the open, against live API calls rather than the system's own reporting. Six endpoints reachable directly - get_clock, get_account, list_positions, list_assets, get_activities, list_orders - and the production ingestor returns a real, complete 30-day batch with zero missing reasons: 11 orders, 12 activities, 21 portfolio-history points. Both apparent failures in my first probe were my own errors, not connectivity: the activity method is get_activities rather than list_activities, and account configurations returns an object rather than a list. Ran the full real path end to end: AlpacaDataGateway.snapshot returned source=alpaca, a live price of 764.38 and all six real positions, then the real qwen3.8:27b produced HOLD at confidence 0.7 and Guardian approved it. The model is genuinely resident on GPU0 at 17.3GB with keep-alive -1, MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0, and answers 174 tokens in 4.40s with speculative decoding at 95% acceptance. Confirmed the LLM is actually in the production loop: 134 llm-sourced decisions on record, 67 of them on the 2026-09-29 session alone, every one model=qwen3.8:27b, ending at market close 15:57:42, with only 2 fallback_policy_engine decisions ever. All three systemd units are active and enabled, loading from durable paths under $HOME/.config/systemd/user with zero enablement links into tmpfs, and the watchdog timer is firing every 10 minutes. Requirement audit against the objective: R1 real, 987 of 987 cycles source=alpaca, no synthetic data. R2 Alpaca link complete, all endpoints plus the production ingestor with zero missing reasons. R3 running and waiting for the open, three units active/enabled/durable with next_open 2026-09-30 09:30 ET. R4 review and confirm, make verify 25 classes 0 failed 1174 test executions exit 0, plus 13 of 13 figures independently reproduced from raw journal text with no production code in the counting path. R5 every previously-reported problem is closed and verified against current state: curriculum truncation fixed with per-site windows 4096/8192 and a 600s timeout, admission bypass closed with zero bypasses, all 31 doctor report names pinned to a failing path, unmanaged exposure reported at $37k or 37 percent of equity, knowledge dedup and prune complete with 2 artifacts 2 distinct lessons and 133 references retained, daemon heartbeat beats on entry to long work, curriculum refusals fed back, and the LLM fallback now surfaced. One item remains open by deliberate choice rather than oversight: shadow mode is wired as a global executor swap rather than a per-strategy stage, so the objective's shadow/probation/promote chain cannot be expressed, and I did not rewrite it because turning a mode flag into a stage defines what evidence a strategy must gather before touching the paper broker, which is the operator's decision. I also found and fixed one new problem today that nothing was reporting: an LLM timeout silently substitutes the deterministic policy engine and the cycle looks ordinary, which is exactly the failure masking the objective forbids, so a new llm fallback check now reports it, escalating on the share rather than the count. I did not raise the 120s timeout, because observed production latency is 24-56s warm with 67 of 67 model-authored decisions, the loop is single-threaded at a 240s interval, and widening it would hide the fallback rather than report it. Commit 031fc90.

Completed the requirement audit the goal rules require and found one item still open, so I resolved it rather than declaring completion. R1 real: 987 of 987 cycles source=alpaca, no synthetic source. R2 Alpaca link complete: 6 of 6 endpoints reachable and the production ingestor returning 11 orders, 12 activities, 21 portfolio-history points with zero missing reasons. R3 running and waiting for the open: ollama, min-agent and quant-watchdog all active and enabled, next_open 2026-09-30 09:30:00-04:00. R4 review and confirm: make verify 26 classes, 0 failed, 1174 test executions across 60 files, exit 0, plus 13 of 13 figures independently reproduced from raw journal text. R5 previous problems: eight closed and verified, plus one more found and closed this turn. That one matters: docs/superpowers/PHASES.md recorded Phase 5 shadow trading as MET citing the shadow-live-consistency class and the live journal, quoting status=SHADOWED and a 920/920 cycle count. The live journal contains zero SHADOWED executions - the status census of all 987 cycles is SKIPPED 908, REJECTED 45, SUBMITTED 34 - MIN_AGENT_SHADOW is off, and the single SHADOW_ORDER_INTENT carries the rationale "shadow stage smoke test". The exit criterion had been marked satisfied by code existing rather than code having run, which is exactly the failure the objective names when it says a configuration, function, test or document existing must never be treated as the feature working, and the phase gate is explicit that the previous phase's exit criteria must be fully met before advancing. Three corrections: the PHASES.md row now reads MECHANISM MET, STAGE NOT RUN with the zero count, the off flag and the smoke-test rationale named; a new shadow-stage-exercised gate reports mechanism and stage separately from the journal so the criterion cannot be read off unit tests, as a WARN rather than a FAIL because a system that has never run shadow is an honest starting state rather than a defect, but it must not be able to say MET; and the gate's own docstring was still carrying the withdrawn claim that shadow is not implemented and the word appears in docstrings only, a falsehood STATUS.md had already withdrawn while it stayed live in tools/verify.py. The stale verification header on the same page reading 21 classes and 614 tests against a gate running 26 is now generated from live output rather than hand-written. verify.py needed a WARN status and did not have one, added with the reasoning attached since only FAIL gates. Three bugs in my own audit script along the way, none of them in the system: all([...]) treated an empty order list as connectivity failure, my next_open grep truncated at the space inside the timestamp, and a gate-line slice came back empty - all corrected and re-run. R6, the single outstanding item: shadow is wired as a global executor swap rather than a per-strategy stage, which decides what evidence a strategy must gather before touching the paper broker and therefore what promotable means. That is an operator decision, not a defect to fix unilaterally, and it is now reported honestly instead of claimed as MET. Commit e82dc18.

Ran one real cycle against the live broker as the strongest pre-open verification - the modified daemon path completed end to end and recorded src=llm model=qwen3.8:27b HOLD qty=0 with Guardian approved and execution SKIPPED, market closed so nothing could trade, and with the model authoring the decision rather than falling back. That turned the gate red twice, on two real latent bugs that had been dormant precisely because the market had not been running long enough to expose them. First, tools/replay_audit.py pinned its expectations at 987 cycles, 34 fills and 33 buys, so one genuine cycle made it red: a check that measures how long it has been since anyone traded is not an accounting check, and a live system's counts grow by design. It now asserts what must hold at any volume - every snapshot broker-sourced, every fill paper-only, submitted <= confirmed, closed lots <= fill events, unmatched sells non-negative - and prints absolute totals for context. The comparison that gives the script its value is restored and computed at runtime: naive FIFO over raw JSON against what the production ledger reports for the same journal right now. Getting it running took four wrong guesses, each turned into a silent "production evaluator unavailable" by a broad except, and a silent fallback inside a check reads as a pass, so it now reports itself as a failure. The guesses: the figures live under .pnl not the top-level result; evaluate() returns MISSING without the broker evidence batch; total_realized_pnl is not on PnLEvidence at all but on the attribution result, a different object from a different module; and unmatched_sell_quantity is per-strategy so the comparable figure is its total. The naive arithmetic stays pure stdlib, with src added to sys.path only so the comparison helper reads the same journal the system reports from. It now confirms closed lots 23, realized 564.39 and unmatched 29.0 by both routes. Second, the replay-determinism check compared every recorded counterfactual row against a fresh recomputation and passed for months because of the defect: no recorded decision had yet gained its 24-hour horizon quote. The first real cycle after a quiet weekend supplied one and the gate went red on a row recorded verdict=PENDING that correctly recomputes as GOOD_HOLD at -0.195005. Measured before changing anything, 0 decided verdicts changed and 1 of 66 PENDING rows had resolved, so the determinism property held throughout and the check was scoring a placeholder. It now skips PENDING rows and prints the resolved-since count rather than swallowing it. Both bugs share a shape worth naming: checks that can only be exercised by the market, where a gate whose green state depends on the absence of data is not a gate and the only way to find that out is to let real data arrive. I also corrected an overstatement of my own in section 45: I had written that the shadow chain cannot be expressed, which is too strong - it is expressible as a manual procedure by flipping the flag, and the narrower true statement is that SHADOWED results never reach the promotion gate so the stage is a dead end for promotion rather than an inexpressible one. make verify 26 classes, 0 failed, 1175 test executions, exit 0. Commit 380a642.
